data.title: Operator Remote-Access / RAT Control Channel
data.summary: The sample exposes a remote-control channel giving the operator interactive access to the host — screen view, file transfer, command execution — equivalent to a legitimate remote-access tool but installed and run covertly.
data.description:
This describes full interactive control rather than a scripted C2 command set: the operator
can browse the filesystem, run arbitrary commands, and often see the desktop live, which is
why capability-wise a RAT of this kind is closer to a legitimate remote-support tool
running without the user's knowledge than to a narrow-purpose implant. Some families
reuse a legitimate remote-access tool's binary wholesale (a 'living off trusted software'
pattern) rather than implementing the channel themselves, trading custom-malware detection
risk for the tool's normally-trusted reputation.
data.recommendation:
* Identify whether the remote-access capability is custom or a repurposed legitimate tool; the latter needs vendor-specific detection and configuration review, not malware signatures.
* Terminate the active session and rotate any credentials or sessions the operator could have observed during interactive access.
* Audit for other legitimate remote-access software installed without a corresponding change-management record, given how often this capability reuses trusted tools.
data.short_recommendation: Determine whether the channel is custom or a repurposed legitimate remote-access tool; the response differs for each.

mitre_techniques.procedure: Installed a bundled copy of a legitimate remote-access tool configured to connect out to operator infrastructure on startup.

mbc_techniques.implementation: Provided the operator full interactive desktop and file-transfer access over an outbound connection.
